newsitem.title: USA: Portec Q2 hurt by recycling business.
newsitem.headline: Portec Q2 hurt by recycling business.

text.p: Portec Inc said Thursday that results in the second quarter continued to be hurt by its Courtec Recycling unit, which supplies conveyor and sorting systems for handling post-consumer recyclables.

Although prices for recycled materials have at least stabilized, or in some cases trended upward, they are still below historical averages, and are deterring capital investment projects in the recycling industry, Portec said.

But the company said its Flomaster specialty conveyor business is performing well, aided by a large order for conveyors from the U.S. Post Office, while its railroad track components business in North America had a strong second quarter, with gains in both sales and operating income over last year.

"(O)ur backlog at June 30, 1997, stood at approximately $22.9 million, nearly 30 percent higher than on June 30, 1996, with increases in each of our three business segments," M.T. Yonker, president and chief executive officer, said in a news release. "This favorable situation should help to offset the typical softness in some of our businesses during the third and fourth quarter."
Earlier Thursday, Portec reported net income of $1.5 million, or $0.34 a share for the second quarter, down from $1.9 million, or $0.42 a share, a year ago.
